original_question: For every classical solution f : [0, T] x R^3 -> [0, infinity) of the space-homogeneous Landau-Coulomb equation with initial data f_0, is the pointwise bound f(t, v) <= sqrt(250 / (9 pi)) max_w f_0(w) valid for all (t, v) in [0, T] x R^3? If true, this would rule out finite-time blow-up through a universal L-infinity estimate.
target_in_paper: Section 7.2, Conjecture 7.3, immediately motivated by Proposition 7.2: a universal L-infinity bound for classical solutions of the 3D space-homogeneous Landau-Coulomb equation.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right section and the right mathematical target: the spatially homogeneous Landau equation with Coulomb kernel in dimension 3, classical nonnegative solutions, the specific universal constant sqrt(250/(9 pi)), quantification for all times and velocities, and the intended consequence that such an estimate would preclude finite-time blow-up.
missing_details: The paper states this as a conjecture, namely Conjecture 7.3 in Section 7.2, not as a proved theorem or a general open-ended question.

The PDE should be written explicitly as the homogeneous equation partial_t f = Q_L(f,f), where Q_L is the 3D Landau-Coulomb collision operator from equation (7.2), rather than referred to only by name.
The dimension d=3 is part of the official formulation and is essential to the constant sqrt(250/(9 pi)).
The constant comes from the three-dimensional evaluation of the universal dimension-only constant in Proposition 7.2; the draft does not say that this is why that exact number appears.

The official formulation is an L-infinity control for every time in the interval of classical existence; your pointwise-in-v wording is equivalent, but it is not tied as explicitly to the paper's formulation.

The surrounding Section 7 tacitly works with classical solutions having sufficient decay as |v| -> infinity when invoking the conservation laws and entropy framework (see note 1); this hidden regularity/decay context is not mentioned.
The authors emphasize that the conjectured bound is independent of the initial mass, momentum, and energy; that feature is part of the intended scope and motivation.

No radial symmetry, monotonicity, or smallness assumptions belong to Conjecture 7.3 itself; those appear only later in the heuristic blow-up discussion and should not be added to the refined question.
refined_question: Let f:[0,T]xR^3->[0,infinity) be a classical solution of the space-homogeneous Landau equation in dimension 3 with Coulomb kernel, namely partial_t f = Q_L(f,f), where Q_L is the Landau-Coulomb operator Q_L(f,f)(v) = div_v int_{R^3} |v-v_*|^(-1) (I - ((v-v_*) tensor (v-v_*))/|v-v_*|^2) (f(v_*) grad_v f(v) - f(v) grad_{v_*} f(v_*)) dv_*, and let f_0(v)=f(0,v). Is it true that every such classical solution satisfies the universal estimate ||f(t,.)||_{L^infty(R^3)} <= sqrt(250/(9 pi)) ||f_0||_{L^infty(R^3)} for every t in [0,T]? In particular, would this dimension-three, mass-momentum-energy-independent L-infinity bound rule out finite-time blow-up for the space-homogeneous Landau-Coulomb equation?
justification: The draft is aiming directly at Conjecture 7.3, not at the later Liouville-type Conjecture 7.5. Proposition 7.2 is the immediate precursor and explains the specific constant by comparing the initial datum with the Maxwellian asymptotic state having the same mass, momentum, and energy. The paragraph right after Conjecture 7.3 states exactly the intended implication: if this universal bound held, it would rule out finite-time blow-up for the homogeneous Landau-Coulomb equation. Section 7 also supplies the hidden notation and scope: the homogeneous equation is partial_t f = Q(f,f), Q is the Landau-Coulomb operator in dimension 3, and the chapter note clarifies the decay-at-infinity convention attached to the classical-solution setting.
